cells.tense: You can decide what's worth keeping and let the rest end without a fight now.
cells.act: hold space for what someone feels without fixing it
cells.ask: When someone close to you gets upset this week, stay there through all of it. Don't fix it, don't solve it, don't cut it short.
cells.core:
You can build things that last and decide when they're done, and the two belong together. The ending doesn't have to be dramatic. You clear what's finished, keep what isn't, and the people near you get to be part of that rather than watch it happen from a distance. What you carry has weight and doesn't crush.

The invitation is to let somebody else in while it's happening. Someone you're close to brings you something they're feeling, and your usual move is to fix it or smooth it over so it's done. Try staying instead. Be there while they're inside it, without steering it anywhere. Being strong for people doesn't have to mean managing what they feel. You can be the place someone lands for a minute this week, and what you're building will hold more because you did.
cells.sheetLine: Strong enough to let something end and still stay.
cells.verb: Deciding what gets built to last and seeing it through
cells.place: At the point where something has to fully end before the next thing can begin

cells.tense: You're deciding what ends before it's even begun, clearing rooms nobody asked you to clear.
cells.act: judge the hurt fairly after it has finished
cells.ask: The next time someone near you is hurt, hold any verdict on whether it's fair. Let them get to the end of it, then call it.
cells.core:
The ending is running out past the season. You catch a whiff of stale and close the thing, and the cleared table feels right from where you sit. From the people near you it reads differently: very little gets to remain long enough to mean something to them. They've stopped showing you what they'd want to keep.

Fairness is the way back in, and fairness has a temper. When something hurts near you, let it run its course before you say whether the hurt holds up. Judge it afterward, not while it's still arriving. The ruling will be shorter for the wait, and whoever it lands on will be able to hear it.
cells.sheetLine: You're cutting things down before they've had a season.
cells.verb: Deciding what gets built to last and seeing it through
cells.place: At the point where something has to fully end before the next thing can begin

cells.tense: You've kept a thing past its end and stood at the threshold a long time without walking through.
cells.act: release what is done and keep what is not
cells.ask: Take one finished thing that's still asking for your hours, and spend those hours on something that has life in it instead.
cells.core:
Something you were carrying has finished, and you're still moving the weight. What held before keeps its slot, and the time goes there out of habit or loyalty, and the thing itself isn't coming back.

This is about knowing what to put down, which isn't the same as quitting. Find one finished thing that's been taking your hours and swap rather than kill: put something with breath in it in that same slot, and go there instead. A piece of work you care about. A walk. Something you've wanted to learn. The slot fills and nobody has to announce anything. You took it to its end, and that's completion, not defeat.
cells.sheetLine: It's finished. Carrying it further isn't strength.
cells.verb: Deciding what gets built to last and seeing it through
cells.place: At the point where something has to fully end before the next thing can begin

cells.tense: You're closing something out with your hands while your mouth says you're not involved in it at all.
cells.act: explore a direction before it has a destination
cells.ask: Follow one thing that interests you this week without deciding where it's headed. No plan, no name for what it becomes.
cells.core:
You keep deciding what ends and what stays. Ask you straight and you'd say you're not doing it, it just turned out that way. But the hands that cleared the space are yours, and the people who watched you do it don't need you to admit it for them to know.

Before the thread you lost was a thread, it was a first move with nothing behind it. Pick something with no promise in it and begin it this week. Not to finish, not to last, just to feel the first move happen. You don't have to name what you're building. A start doesn't owe anyone a finish. Your gift for holding things to the end is real, and it doesn't disappear when you follow something with no ending already in mind.
cells.sheetLine: You end things by hand, even unsigned.
cells.verb: Deciding what gets built to last and seeing it through
cells.place: At the point where something has to fully end before the next thing can begin
